title: Geometric interpretation of non-equal weights in Ceva theorem

problemStatement.formal: weight_division_ratio : (D - B) / (C - D) = β / α where D = (α * B + β * C) / (α + β)
problemStatement.plain: The weight parameters (α, β) in Ceva's theorem encode the division ratio of the cevian point: D = (α·B + β·C)/(α+β) divides BC in ratio BD:DC = β:α.
whyMatters: Explains the geometric meaning of the algebraic weight parameters in Ceva's theorem
Shows equal weights give midpoints (centroid), angle-bisector weights give incenter
Establishes precise criterion for which side D is closer to

proven: Division ratio BD/DC = β/α for D = (α·B + β·C)/(α+β)
Midpoint iff α = β (when B ≠ C)
D closer to B iff β < α
